text: 中年人如何创业？
en: How should middle-aged people start a business?

text: 1. 不熟不做。
en: 1. Don't do what you don't know well.

text: 不是自己足够了解的行业不做。
en: Don't go into an industry you don't know well enough.

text: 2. 做自己最擅长的、能变现的创业项目。
en: 2. Work on the startup projects you are best at and that can be monetised.

text: 创业赚钱，与情怀、兴趣的关联度很小，中年人需要养家糊口、上有老下有小，必须更现实一些。
en: Making money through entrepreneurship has little to do with ideals or interests; middle-aged people need to support their families, with elderly parents above and young children below, so they must be more pragmatic.

text: 中年人创业，做自己擅长的、而且能够短期变现的创业项目。
en: For middle-aged entrepreneurs, work on projects you are good at and that can be monetised in the short term.

text: 一个创业项目，如果长期不能变现，或者变现很难，这样的创业项目就不要去碰了。
en: If a startup project cannot be monetised over the long term, or is very hard to monetise, then stay away from such projects.

text: 3. 看好的行业，哪怕再了解、再有信心，有条件的话，还是先去这个行业工作3-6个月。
en: 3. For an industry you favour, even if you understand it well and feel confident, if you have the means, it is best to first work in that industry for three to six months.

text: 建议最好是去类似的行业/公司，兼职或者专职上班几个月，提前摸一摸行业的实际情况。
en: It is best to work for a few months in a similar industry or company, either part-time or full-time, to get a feel for the actual situation of the industry in advance.

text: 中产创业，死亡率最高的就是一头扎进某个新领域的创业新手，这是妥妥的韭菜！
en: Among middle-class entrepreneurs, those with the highest failure rate are newcomers who plunge headlong into some new field — they are absolute suckers!

text: 同时，创业者可以找一下身边的创业成功者（或者还活着的创业者）多聊聊，看看会有哪些坑，哪些注意事项，多咨询一下。
en: At the same time, entrepreneurs can seek out successful entrepreneurs around them (or those still surviving in business) to chat with, to learn what pitfalls and precautions there are, and to consult more.

text: 了解更透彻一些，然后再决定是否自己创业。
en: Gain a deeper understanding, and then decide whether to start your own business.

text: 4. 不要借贷太多资金。
en: 4. Do not borrow too much capital.

text: 中年人创业，提前衡量自己能够承受的最大亏损额，尽量不要借钱创业、负债创业、银行贷款创业；中年人创业，尽量选择相对较小的启动资金（自有资金），然后找一些投资人、股东的钱进来，但是不让他们参与具体经营，提前讲好就可以了。
en: For middle-aged entrepreneurs, assess in advance the maximum loss you can bear; try not to start a business with borrowed money, with debt, or with bank loans. For middle-aged entrepreneurs, choose a relatively small amount of start-up capital (your own funds) where possible, then bring in money from some investors or shareholders, but do not let them take part in day-to-day management — just agree on this in advance.

text: 5. 安顿好家人。
en: 5. Settle your family well.

text: 给家人留下足够的正常生活开支，解决创业者自身的“后顾之忧”。
en: Leave your family enough for their normal living expenses, so as to resolve the entrepreneur's own 'domestic concerns'.

text: 创业者没有后顾之忧，则会心安，心安就能全身心的投入到创业事业中来。
en: If an entrepreneur has no such domestic concerns, they will be at peace; with peace of mind, they can devote themselves wholly to the entrepreneurial endeavour.

text: “家和万事兴”，中年人创业，首先就要理解和解决好这一点。
en: 'Harmony in the family brings success in all things' — for middle-aged entrepreneurs, the first step is to understand and resolve this point.

text: 6. 选择的创业项目，一开始就准备干10年甚至更长时间，这样会更有规划性、更有目的性、更有条理性、更有持久战斗力。
en: 6. For the startup project you choose, prepare from the very beginning to work at it for ten years or even longer; this will give you more planning, more purpose, more order, and more staying power.

text: 中年人创业，很多时候我们也就是一次创业机会了。
en: For middle-aged entrepreneurs, more often than not we only get one chance to start a business.

text: 真要是错过了一次好的创业机会，再想有第二次创业的机会，可能都不现实了。
en: If you truly miss one good entrepreneurial opportunity, the idea of a second chance may no longer be realistic.

text: 所以，中年人创业，要选择那些能干5年、10年甚至一辈子的创业事业。
en: Therefore, middle-aged entrepreneurs should choose entrepreneurial endeavours they can pursue for five years, ten years, or even a lifetime.

text: 7. 吃不了苦的人，别创业（无论什么行业）。
en: 7. Those who cannot endure hardship should not start a business (in any industry).

text: 这种苦包括精神和肉体的苦。
en: This hardship includes both mental and physical suffering.

text: 创业，并不是每个人都适合的；有些人真的吃不了创业的苦，那就省省心，别创业了。
en: Entrepreneurship is not for everyone; some people genuinely cannot bear its hardships, so they should spare themselves the worry and not start a business.

text: 8. 坚定的相信自己。
en: 8. Firmly believe in yourself.

text: 无比自信的相信自己，相信自己的未来会更好，相信自己会有更璀璨的明天和命运。
en: Believe in yourself with absolute confidence; believe that your future will be better, and that you will have a brighter tomorrow and destiny.

text: 相信“相信的力量”。
en: Believe in 'the power of believing'.

text: 舍我其谁！
en: If not me, then who?!

text: 任何时候，永远不要放弃相信自己！
en: At any time, never give up believing in yourself!

text: 中年人创业，就是一条不归路，要么创业干成功，创业就变成一辈子的事业；要么创业干失败，可能这一辈子就结束了。
en: For middle-aged entrepreneurs, starting a business is a point of no return: either you succeed and entrepreneurship becomes your life's work, or you fail and that may well be the end of everything.

text: 中年人创业，是没有回头路可走的。
en: For middle-aged entrepreneurs, there is no road back.

text: 9. 中年人创业，在正式创业前，一定要认真请教、咨询有过创业实战经验的创业者，尤其是正能量多的成功创业者，这些人的创业经验教训，能减少中年创业者巨大的金钱损失，规避创业中的各种坑。
en: 9. Before formally starting a business, middle-aged entrepreneurs must earnestly seek advice from those with real entrepreneurial experience, especially successful entrepreneurs full of positive energy; the lessons of such people can save middle-aged entrepreneurs enormous financial losses and help them avoid the various pitfalls of entrepreneurship.

text: 作者简介：20多年创业和管理培训，专注于创业咨询、教育咨询，欢迎交流探讨xiongxiaozixun。
en: About the author: over 20 years of entrepreneurship and management training, focused on startup consultancy and education consultancy; welcome to exchange ideas via xiongxiaozixun.

text: 原本苦心经营的东西突然变得不再那么重要
en: The things one once painstakingly nurtured suddenly become less important.

text: 相信自己的直觉和判断力就是人生最优解
en: Trusting one's own intuition and judgement is the optimal solution in life.

text: 活了半辈子是个里程碑 尚能开新篇
en: Having lived half a lifetime is a milestone, and one can still begin a new chapter.

text: What was once painstakingly cultivated suddenly becomes less important.
en: What was once painstakingly cultivated suddenly becomes less important.

text: Trusting my instincts and judgment is the optimal solution in life.
en: Trusting my instincts and judgment is the optimal solution in life.

text: Living half a lifetime is a milestone, but it can also mark the beginning of a new chapter.
en: Living half a lifetime is a milestone, but it can also mark the beginning of a new chapter.

text: 波叔在收到小米5年工作金米兔纪念之际，申请转岗到了销售体系的GTM部门，或者叫销售运营部门，这是关于这次转岗的一些思考。
en: On receiving Xiaomi's five-year 'Golden Mi Tu' service commemorative award, Bo Shu applied for a transfer to the sales system's GTM department, also known as the sales operations department; these are some reflections on that transfer.

text: 凡是过往，皆为序章
en: All that is past is but a prologue.

text: 波叔2018年在小米上市前夕加入小米的国际业务部，先后负责小米生态链和手机产品的国际产品规划工作，俗称产品经理。
en: In 2018, shortly before Xiaomi's listing, Bo Shu joined Xiaomi's international business department, where he successively led the international product planning for Xiaomi's ecosystem chain and mobile phone products, commonly known as a product manager.

text: 在小米工作5年也是波叔在一个公司最长的一段履历，当然之前职业变化基本都是公司的业务调整引起，比如摩托罗拉，诺基亚，黑莓，乐视等等，现在手机行业除了三星苹果全是国内企业在做了。
en: The five years at Xiaomi is also the longest tenure Bo Shu has had at any single company. Of course, his earlier career changes were basically caused by corporate business adjustments — such as Motorola, Nokia, BlackBerry, LeTV, and so on. Today, apart from Samsung and Apple, the mobile phone industry is entirely made up of domestic companies.

text: 在小米5年的工作中，赶上中国产品出海和小米海外业务快速发展的黄金时期，波叔推动了一些爆款产品的出海，为国际用户提供了一些好产品，这些产品也为小米的海外业务贡献几百个小目标。
en: During his five years at Xiaomi, he caught the golden period of Chinese products going global and Xiaomi's rapid overseas expansion. Bo Shu promoted the international launch of several hit products, providing good products to international users, and these products also contributed several hundred small targets to Xiaomi's overseas business.

text: 个人方面也很高兴的经历了孩子的出生和陪伴成长，总体而言，过去的5年对于波叔也是持续成长，不断收获的5年。
en: On a personal level, he was also glad to experience the birth of his child and to accompany them as they grew; overall, the past five years were also a period of continuous growth and constant reward for Bo Shu.

text: 现在工作干得挺好，挺稳定的，为什么要转岗？
en: The work now is going quite well and is fairly stable, so why seek a transfer?

text: 首先是公司有好的制度，鼓励转岗，鼓励跨部门流动。
en: First, the company has a good system that encourages transfers and cross-department mobility.

text: 转岗对公司和个人都是一个风险投资，转岗需要适应期，短则半年，长的可能一年以上。
en: A transfer is a risky venture for both the company and the individual; it requires an adjustment period — as short as half a year, or possibly more than a year.

text: 比如你在原岗位已经是一个表现突出的，有85分以上的表现，表现不好的也不允许转岗。
en: For example, you must already be a standout performer in your original role, scoring above 85; those who perform poorly are not allowed to transfer.

text: 转岗到新的岗位，一开始可能只能做到50分的输出，个人能不能在新的岗位上做到优秀需要个人学习与新岗位的适应。
en: After transferring to a new post, you may only be able to deliver at a 50-point level at first; whether you can excel in the new role depends on your own learning and adaptation to it.

text: 转岗后如果不适应，对公司而言，不只是少了一个原来能稳定输出价值的员工，也是巨大的机会成本，毕竟同一个岗位可能有更适合的任选，为了培养你适应岗位浪费了一年的时间，让跟你一起工作的同事需要花更多的时间支持你。
en: If you fail to adapt after the transfer, for the company it means not only losing an employee who could steadily deliver value, but also a huge opportunity cost. After all, there may be a more suitable candidate for that same post; a year is wasted training you to fit the role, and your colleagues who work with you have to spend more time supporting you.

text: 成功的转岗，对公司而言，也能收获一个综合性的人才，越是靠近用户，面临越多的不确定性，越需要综合性人才，所以不只是小米，很多公司都鼓励之字形人才发展，就是让员工具备跨体系的视野和综合能力。
en: A successful transfer also yields a versatile talent for the company. The closer one is to users and the more uncertainty one faces, the more versatile talent is needed. Therefore, not only Xiaomi but many companies encourage zigzag talent development — that is, giving employees a cross-system perspective and comprehensive ability.

text: 对于个人而言，转岗就是换行，换赛道，根据转岗的跨度不同，难易程度也不一样，对个人发展也是一个很大的不确定性。
en: For the individual, a transfer means changing trades and switching tracks; the difficulty varies with the span of the transfer, and it is also a great uncertainty for personal development.

text: 转岗能拓展个人事业宽度，但是很多工作要从比较初级的开始，如果一直跟不上业务的发展，个人也很难有好的发展，导致转岗失败，对个人也是巨大的机会成本。
en: A transfer can broaden one's career scope, but much of the work starts from a relatively junior level; if you keep failing to keep pace with the business, it will be hard to develop well, leading to a failed transfer — also a huge opportunity cost for the individual.

text: 所以转岗要慎重。
en: So transfers should be approached with caution.

text: 当然要在换工作的时候转岗更是难上加难，因为企业肯定希望以最低风险找到最合适的人选，而不是冒险找另外一个正在冒险转岗的人。
en: Of course, transferring while also changing jobs is even more difficult, because a company will certainly want to find the most suitable person at the lowest risk, rather than taking a chance on someone who is already taking a chance by transferring.

text: 其次是随着业务的熟悉，学习曲线进入到平台期，很难有大的突破，持续这种状态会影响工作的热情。
en: Next, as you grow familiar with the work, the learning curve plateaus, making major breakthroughs hard; sustained in this state, your enthusiasm for the work will suffer.

text: 怎么判断这种状态，就是看日常工作里面是不是有越来越多重复性的工作，很多事情凭经验判断就八九不离十的感觉，好的一面这是熟悉业务可以稳定输出价值的状态，不好的一面是容易对工作失去热情。
en: How do you recognise this state? Look at whether your daily work contains more and more repetitive tasks, and whether many things can be judged with experience and feel 'pretty much certain'. The good side is that this is a state of knowing the business well enough to deliver stable value; the bad side is that it easily drains your enthusiasm for the work.

text: 当然这方面在不同的人也会有不同的应对，可能很多人对于把工作做到60分就满意，多做就觉得浪费，有的人觉得85分就是已经超过绝大多数了，还有一些对工作自我要求很高的人，要做到95分才满意。
en: Of course, different people respond to this differently: many are satisfied with doing work at a 60-point level and feel doing more is a waste; some feel that 85 points already puts them above the vast majority; and a few who hold themselves to a high standard are only satisfied at 95 points.

text: 不管怎么样，达到预期的结果后，难免热情下降。
en: However it is, once the expected results are achieved, a drop in enthusiasm is hard to avoid.

text: 就像一个球队，把所有能拿的顶级赛事冠军都拿遍了，跟那些没拿过冠军的相比，对胜利和冠军的饥渴感是不一样的，所以在竞争激烈的足球世界杯，欧洲杯，冠军杯等等顶级赛事上面很难看到卫冕成功的。
en: It is like a football team that has won every top trophy available: compared with teams that have never won a championship, their hunger for victory and titles is different. That is why in fiercely contested top tournaments such as the football World Cup, the European Championship, and the Champions League, it is rare to see a successful defence of a title.

text: 最后和最重要的一个，还是看个人兴趣。
en: Last, and most important, it comes down to personal interest.

text: 做自己感兴趣的事情是一件大部分人很向往，但是实际做起来比较难的事情。
en: Doing what interests you is something most people aspire to, yet is fairly hard to actually do.

text: 一个是看是不是有合适的时机，更重要的是愿不愿意承担做选择的代价，特别是一个有家庭，有相对稳定工作的状态，要冒险去做改变对大部分人还是不容易的事情，小到个人，大到企业调整业务，国家改革都是类似的情况。
en: One aspect is whether the timing is right; more important is whether one is willing to bear the cost of choosing. Especially when one has a family and a relatively stable job, taking a risk to make a change is still not easy for most people. From individuals at the small scale to companies adjusting their business and nations reforming at the large scale, the situation is similar.

text: 但是如果放到人生的长度去思考，短期转岗的阵痛其实不算大事，所谓行则将至，如果畏难不去做尝试，可能是一直的遗憾。
en: But if you think in terms of the length of a whole life, the short-term pain of a transfer is not really a big deal. As the saying goes, 'walking will get you there'; if you shrink from difficulty and never try, it may become a lasting regret.

text: 波叔的兴趣是希望到更靠近业务，能更近的感受业务起伏的地方。
en: Bo Shu's interest is to be closer to the business, where he can feel its ups and downs more directly.

text: 这方面不同的人会有很大的差别，就像打仗，有的人比较享受像张良一样在大后方运筹帷幄，有的人就喜欢像韩信一样在战场上拼杀，有的人就喜欢像萧何一样把粮草辎重安排的明明白白的。
en: People differ greatly on this, much like in war: some enjoy orchestrating strategy from the rear like Liang Zhang, some prefer fighting on the battlefield like Xin Han, and some like to arrange supplies and provisions meticulously like He Xiao.

text: 下一步怎么办？
en: What next?

text: 波叔叫叔真不是倚老卖老，现在00后已经进入职场，身边也有00左右的同事一起共事，客气的同事叫波哥，熟悉的同事就叫波叔了。
en: 'Uncle Bo' is really not a case of trading on seniority; now those born after 2000 have entered the workplace, and there are colleagues around him born around that time. Polite colleagues call him 'Brother Bo', while familiar ones call him 'Uncle Bo'.

text: 怎么样跟这些年轻的优秀同事工作，波叔首先是没有心理负担的，就是开放心态，对事不对人，重要的是能不能学到技能加深认知，其他的不重要，就像很多大佬说的，别把自己太当回事儿，别人没那么在乎你是谁。
en: As for how to work with these young and excellent colleagues, Bo Shu first carries no psychological burden: he keeps an open mind and focuses on the matter, not the person. What matters is whether he can learn skills and deepen his understanding; everything else is unimportant. As many big shots say, don't take yourself too seriously — others care far less about who you are.

text: 所以最重要的肯定是持续学习打怪升级，在做中练做中学。
en: So the most important thing is surely to keep learning and levelling up, practising through doing and learning through doing.

text: GTM除了日常跟其他部门同事流程性对接，最重要的是预测未来的能力，在很多不确定性条件下做复杂决策的能力，经常要决策未来一年的事情，是一个比较依赖经验的工作。
en: Besides the day-to-day procedural coordination with colleagues in other departments, the most important part of GTM is the ability to forecast the future and to make complex decisions under many uncertain conditions; it often requires deciding things a year ahead, and is a job that relies fairly heavily on experience.

text: 基于波叔的经验，行业洞察力，可能可以从60分起步，更快的启动跟上业务发展需求。
en: Based on Bo Shu's experience and industry insight, he may be able to start from a 60-point level and ramp up faster to meet the needs of business development.

text: 这个话题还得持续复盘总结更新，可能随着认识的加深还会有不同或者跟现在完全相反的看法。
en: This topic still needs to be continuously reviewed, summarised, and updated; as understanding deepens, views may change or even turn completely opposite to those held now.

text: 路虽远，行则将至
en: Though the road is long, those who walk will arrive.
